dva-avc-025.text: A development team is building a collaborative whiteboard application in real time, where multiple users instantly see each other's design actions. Frequent polling at sub-second intervals generates a massive number of calls from API (proportional to the number of customers × polling frequency), at significant cost and still introducing up to 500ms latency per event — this does not provide the two-way experience 'instant'/almost real-time and is a known anti-standard compared to WebSockets.

dva-avc-029.text: A function AWS Lambda processes rows of records Amazon SQS calling 'UpdateItem' in Amazon DynamoDB (Table in provided capacity mode) for each record, within a sequential loop. dva-avc-034.text: An e-commerce system stores the stock quantity of each product in an 'stockcount' attribute of an item of the Amazon DynamoDB. optionRationales: Correct. Incorrect. This classic pattern of 'read, check in code, then write' is vulnerable to a race condition (race condition): two competing invocations can both run 'GetItem' and read 'stockCount'=1' ANTES that anyone executes 'PutItem', both check 'greater than zero' successfully, and both record 'stockCount'=0' — resulting in two sales for only one unit in stock.

Incorrect. DynamoDB does not support operations of 'JOIN' between tables — combining data from two tables would require multiple calls from API and combination logic in the application, in addition to a significant migration of the existing data model, to solve something that 'ProjectionExpression' solves with a single additional parameter in the existing call.

DAX reduces the reading LATENCIA REPETIDAS of the MESMO item (cache hits), but does not reduce the TAMANHO of the returned/deserialized data for each single item — for users first accessed (cache miss) or for a listing with many different users, the complete item would still be returned and deserialized, not addressing the root cause of the problem..

Incorrect. Scan read to TABELA INTEIRA (consuming reading capacity proportional to TODOS the items in the table) regardless of the filter or projection applied — this is significantly more inefficient than a directed 'GetItem'/'Query', and does not meet the objective of reducing the returned payload per item efficiently..

dva-avc-036.text: A team is integrating a API REST of the Amazon API Gateway with a function AWS Lambda existing, which is written to receive directly a simplified event object in the format '{ "userId": "...", "action": "..." }'. API Gateway is configured with proxy integration Lambda' (Lambda proxy integration), and the function is failing because, instead of the expected simplified object, it receives the standard proxy envelope (containing heads, queryStringParameters, body as string, etc.), with simplified payload nested within event.body as a string JSON.
options: Configure an application/json 'Binary Media Type' in the API Gateway.

Switch to 'customized integration' Lambda' (Lambda custom integration) with a requisition mapping template (VTL) which extracts 'userId' and 'action' from the body of the request and sends them as the event directly to the Lambda.
Update function code Lambda to make parse (ex.: 'JSON.parse') of 'event.body', extracting the simplified object '{ userId, action }' from inside it before using it.
Add one Lambda Authorize in front of the function to transform the body of the requisition before invoking the main function.
dva-avc-036.explanation: Right. In the proxy integration. Lambda', o API Gateway SEMPRE involves the requisition in a standard envelope (headers, parameters, and the body of the original requisition as string in 'event.body'), regardless of the shape of the body sent by the client; the correct and recommended adjustment is to make the parse of 'event.body' within the function itself, in the function programming language — simpler approach to test and maintain than mapping templates.
dva-avc-036.hint: Think about how proxy integration Lambda of the API Gateway structures the event received by the function, and where within this structure the original body of the customer's request is placed.
optionRationales: Right. In the proxy integration. Lambda', o API Gateway SEMPRE involves the requisition in a standard envelope (headers, parameters, and the body of the original requisition as string in 'event.body'), regardless of the shape of the body sent by the client; the correct and recommended adjustment is to make the parse of 'event.body' within the function itself, in the function programming language — simpler approach to test and maintain than mapping templates.

Incorrect. Although technically possible, this requires writing and maintaining templates VTL (Velocity Template Language) — a separate template language, with limited debugging and testing — to achieve something that is solved in a simpler and more straightforward way by parseing 'event.body' into the function code itself, in the language that the team already uses; it is an unnecessary operational complexity for this requirement.

Incorrect. 'Binary Media Types' control how API Gateway treats binary payloads (e.g. images, base encoding64) for non-textual content types — setting this to 'application/json' has no effect on how the proxy integration event envelope is structured when passed to function Lambda, and does not solve the incompatibility of format described.

Incorrect. Lambda Authorizers are designed to take decisions on AUTHENTICATION/AUTORIZATION (returning a policy) IAM and, optionally, an additional context) — they do not replace or transform the body of the requisition ('event.body') that the main integration function receives; using an autorizer for payload transformation is not a standard supported for that purpose.
